elements.content: Communication Goal: I can ask about habits, talk about what people do and do not do, and express likes and dislikes.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 4. People and Likes
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: People and Likes
- Materials: Habit grid, preference scale, interview cards, profile frames.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use present simple negatives
• ask Do/Does and Wh- questions
• express preferences with object pronouns

Prior learning: Recycles present simple and frequency adverbs.

Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

free time — time when you are not working. Example: I read in my free time.
hobby — an activity you enjoy in free time. Example: My hobby is reading.
podcast — an audio show you listen to online. Example: I listen to podcasts on my commute.
music — sounds made with voices or instruments. Example: We listen to music together.
gym — a place for exercise. Example: I go to the gym twice a week.
walk — to move on foot. Example: I walk to work.
video call — a call with sound and video. Example: We have a video call at ten.
read — to look at and understand words. Example: I read every evening.
sleep — to rest with your eyes closed. Example: I sleep eight hours.
cooking — making food. Example: He loves cooking.
traveling — going from one place to another. Example: I love traveling.
shopping — buying things in shops. Example: I go shopping on Saturday.
running — moving quickly on foot. Example: I go running three times a week.
crowded — full of people. Example: The metro is crowded at rush hour.
spicy — having a strong hot taste. Example: The curry is very spicy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I don't drink coffee after two. (present simple negative)
• He doesn't eat meat. (third-person negative)
• Do you listen to podcasts? — Yes, I do. (yes/no question)
• Does your partner work on weekends? — No, she doesn't. (third-person question)
• Where do you usually have lunch? (wh- question)
• I love cooking, and I don't mind cleaning up. (preference + -ing)
• Action movies? I love them. (object pronoun)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'time when you are not working'?
Which word means 'an activity you enjoy in free time'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Do/Does weak forms and -ing endings

Do you /də jə/ — weak form in questions
Does she /dʌz ʃi/ — clear /z/
cooking /ˈkʊkɪŋ/ — stress the first syllable
traveling /ˈtrævəlɪŋ/ — three syllables
Listen and repeat:
Do you listen to podcasts? Does she work on weekends? I love cooking, and I don't mind cleaning up.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use the present simple for habits, routines, facts, and things that happen regularly.

Form:
Present simple: I / You / We / They + verb. He / She / It + verb + -s. Negative: don't / doesn't + verb. Question: Do / Does + subject + verb?

Examples:
• I work in a school.
• She works in a hospital.
• We don't work on Sunday.
• Does he drink coffee?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
He ___ tea every morning.
They ___ in a hospital.
She ___ like coffee.
___ you work here?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I ... (work / study / live) in ...
• He ... (work / study / live) in ...
• They ... (don't / doesn't) ... on Sunday.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you do every day?
• Where does your best friend work or study?
• Do you drink coffee in the morning?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your daily routine.
• Write three sentences about a family member's routine.
Reading: People and Likes

Question of the week: What do you do to relax after work? Hannah loves cooking. She cooks dinner every evening and listens to music. She hates watching TV. Lucas goes running three times a week. He doesn't like running in the rain, so he uses the gym. Mei likes reading mystery books and listening to podcasts. She visits her parents once a week on Sundays.
Does Hannah watch TV every evening?
How often does Lucas go running?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Do you drink coffee in the morning?
B: Yes, I do. Usually two cups before noon.
A: Do you cook at home during the week?
B: No, I don't. I finish work late, so I usually buy dinner.
A: How often do you exercise?
B: Twice a week. I swim on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
A: What do you like doing on weekends?
B: I love hiking with friends, and I don't mind cleaning on Sunday afternoons.
Does the speaker cook on weekdays?
How often does the speaker exercise?
Speaking task: Interview your partner about habits, free time, and preferences. Use Do/Does and one object pronoun.

• What do you do to relax?
• Do you listen to podcasts?
• Does your family cook on Sundays?
• What do you love doing?
• What do you hate doing?
Role-play: You are hosting a mini-podcast. Ask five questions about your guest's habits and preferences, then report two answers to the group.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about a partner's habits and preferences using he/she, doesn't, and one object pronoun.
Model: She likes ... She doesn't ... She does it because ... I like them too.
